Modern.vision: A label whose 50th release will still be on the same imprint, the same vinyl spec, the same care.

Modern.manifesto: Most modern labels release directly to streaming and treat vinyl as merchandise. We started Stylus because the actual best record is still the physical artefact — the sleeve, the inner sleeve, the liner notes, the moment of dropping the needle. Vinyl first. Streaming second.
Modern.industrySummary: Independent record labels have matured into recognized cohorts around genre and era. The opening is for a smaller, considered label that treats vinyl as the primary release format rather than a secondary collector's edition, with a deliberate release cadence.

Luxury.tagline: A music publisher and label. Established 1959.

Beaufort Music House works across:

• Heritage classical and jazz catalog stewardship
• Limited deluxe physical editions of catalog works
• Annual private salon concerts for subscribers

Luxury.vision: A house whose 100th anniversary in 2059 is celebrated by the descendants of its founding artists.
coreValues: Senior — publishing decisions are made by the director, in person.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Beaufort is a real English surname with a long-established register in publishing and the arts (Beaufort family, ducal English aristocracy). Music House follows the heritage publishing convention (Boosey & Hawkes, Schirmer, Universal Edition tradition). The pair places the brand firmly in the serious-music heritage publisher tradition.
Luxury.manifesto: Most modern record labels are content companies. Beaufort Music House is a publisher first — the rights, the catalog, the artist's interests across decades. We were founded in 1959 and we are still owned by the founding family. The roster grows by referral and is capped at twenty-four living artists. The catalog grows by stewardship.
Luxury.industrySummary: Heritage classical and jazz publishers have consolidated under a small number of global firms (Universal Music Publishing, Sony Music Publishing, Boosey & Hawkes within Concord). There is a quieter market for the small independent music house in continuous family ownership with a long-arc roster.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Boosey & Hawkes (boosey.com) holds the heritage classical-publishing reference. Verve Records (vervelabelgroup.com) sits in the heritage jazz peer slot. ECM Records (ecmrecords.com) plays the considered-modern peer position. Edition Peters (editionpeters.com) is the heritage publishing reference. We belong alongside ECM with a stronger publishing-house register.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Beaufort Music House is a heritage independent music publisher and label in continuous family operation since 1959, with twenty-four living artists and a deep classical and jazz catalog.
Luxury.positioningRationale: We do not extend the roster. The house is the limit. Artists are accepted by referral; the publishing relationship is the long arc.

Creative.mission: To make records the way the records we love were made — analog from input to vinyl groove.
Creative.vision: A label whose tenth-anniversary box set is still pressed from the original tape masters in 2035.
coreValues: Specific — the signal chain is part of the record.
Considered — every session is documented.
Warm — analog sounds are an aesthetic choice, not a flaw.
Slightly nerdy — depth in the craft is the point.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Tape Hiss is the audible artefact of analog magnetic tape recording — a real engineering trade phrase. As a label name it stakes a position against digital-first production. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school (Stones Throw, Daptone register).
Creative.manifesto: Most modern music is digital from microphone to ear. We started The Tape Hiss Co because the actual best records were tracked on tape, mixed on a console, mastered to vinyl, and the audible signature of that chain — the small noise floor, the tape compression, the warmth — is the work, not a flaw. The label exists to make those records.
Creative.industrySummary: Analog music production has become a recognized craft niche with dedicated studios and engineers. There is real space for a label that specializes entirely in analog-tracked work and positions around the technical chain as the creative argument.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Third Man Records (thirdmanrecords.com) is the closest peer in analog-craft positioning. Daptone Records (daptonerecords.com) holds the heritage-analog peer slot. Numero Group (numerogroup.com) sits in the reissue-craft middle. Mexican Summer (mexicansummer.com) plays in the considered-modern indie position. We sit alongside Third Man with a stricter analog-only signal chain.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Tape Hiss Co is a music label releasing only records recorded, mixed, and mastered entirely on analog equipment.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the technical chain. Every record on the label is documented with its full signal chain — tape stock, console model, monitor pair, mastering chain — printed on the sleeve.

targetAudience.primary: Music listeners 28-55 who care about how records sound and how they're made.
behaviors: Buy records for the recording quality.
Read engineering credits.
Own audio equipment they've maintained for years.
Re-buy classic records on new analog masters.
motivations: Want records made the old way, on purpose.
Want a label whose technical decisions they trust.

dos: Print the signal chain on every sleeve.
Photograph the studio gear, not the artist.
Write liner notes about the recording session.
Reference engineers by name.
donts: No remastering of analog originals through digital processing.

messagingPillars.name: Analog signal chain
messagingPillars.description: Every record on the label is tracked, mixed, and mastered on analog equipment. The full signal chain is printed on the sleeve.

messagingPillars.name: Studio operations
messagingPillars.description: The label operates its own analog recording studio. Outside artists can rent the studio for analog-only sessions.

messagingPillars.name: First year on vinyl and cassette only
messagingPillars.description: Every release ships first on vinyl and cassette. Streaming distribution begins 12 months after the physical release.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Tape Hiss Co set in a hand-drawn display serif with a small illustration of a reel-to-reel tape machine beside it. The mark feels printed on a vintage recording-studio matchbook.

colorPalette.name: Tape
colorPalette.meaning: Primary — the colour of magnetic tape oxide.

colorPalette.name: Reel
colorPalette.meaning: Secondary — the colour of a console face.

typography.primary: A hand-drawn display serif for the wordmark and album titles.
typography.secondary: A typewriter mono for the signal-chain credits on sleeves.
typography.rationale: The serif sets the warm-craft tone. The mono signals 'this is engineering.'
